details: Houthi rebels have escalated attacks in Yemen's oil-rich Marib province, killing at least five people, including government forces and civilians. Simultaneously, Houthi-blamed attacks in Saudi Arabia's southern Najran region injured 11 civilians. A military source close to the Saudi army stated that the Saudi-led coalition would not "stand idly by" as the Houthis increase their aggression, signaling a potential for further conflict in the Arabian Peninsula. This comes after one of the deadliest days in the Yemeni civil war, with 58 government troops killed in missile and drone attacks attributed to the Houthis.
title: Houthi attacks intensify in Yemen's Marib, Saudi Arabia's Najran.

details: Tehran has indicated that a deal with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global oil shipments, is nearing finalization. This diplomatic breakthrough, largely facilitated by Oman, aims to resolve shipping bottlenecks that have plagued the region amid ongoing tensions. While the specific technical protocols and terms regarding security patrols or fees are not yet fully disclosed, the agreement could lead to a return to stability for global energy corridors, though the United States has set conditions for its support, emphasizing guaranteed free passage for all vessels.
title: Iran, Oman close to agreement on reopening vital Strait of Hormuz.

details: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have signed a significant joint defense agreement in Mecca, committing to treat an armed attack against any one signatory as an attack against all three. This pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and expand defense cooperation, building on a previous Saudi-Pakistan bilateral agreement from September 2025. This new alliance is a major development in regional power dynamics and could reshape security architecture in the wider Middle East and South Asia.
title: New trilateral defense pact forged between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan.

details: The conflict between Russia and Ukraine has intensified across the Black Sea, with both sides increasing military operations targeting maritime routes, ports, and military assets. Russian forces have stepped up strikes on vessels in shipping corridors intended for international cargo, particularly Ukrainian agricultural exports. Ukraine has also expanded its naval operations, targeting ships in the Sea of Azov to disrupt Russian supply lines. This escalation raises concerns about global food markets and maritime commerce.
title: Black Sea conflict intensifies, threatening shipping and grain exports.
